title: Team and projects
description: Who is on which team, who owns which project and task, what depends on what, what was decided in which meeting, and what the risks are. For product, engineering or client work.

entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: An individual who works on or with the team. Not for: teams (Team) or companies (Organization). Examples: 'Marta Ruiz', 'client contact Jorge'.

entity_types.name: Team
entity_types.description: A group of people working together inside an organization. Use for: squads, departments, working groups. Not for: the whole company (Organization). Examples: 'Platform team', 'Design guild'.

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.description: A company or institution outside or above the team. Use for: customers, partners, vendors, the employer. Not for: a team inside the company (Team) or a person. Examples: 'Acme Corp', 'Customer: Globex'.

entity_types.name: Project
entity_types.description: A bounded initiative with a goal and an expected end, usually with several tasks. Not for: single tasks (Task) or recurring operations. Examples: 'Mobile app v2', 'Data migration'.

entity_types.name: Task
entity_types.description: A concrete unit of work assigned to someone, with a clear outcome. Use for: tickets, issues, to-dos. Not for: whole projects or goals. Examples: 'Write the API spec', 'Fix login timeout'.

entity_types.name: Milestone
entity_types.description: A dated checkpoint or deliverable in a project. Not for: ordinary tasks (Task) or whole projects. Examples: 'Beta release 2026-06-30', 'Contract signed'.

entity_types.name: Meeting
entity_types.description: A scheduled gathering with attendees and usually decisions or actions. Not for: ongoing channels or one-person events. Examples: 'Sprint review 42', 'Kick-off with Globex'.

entity_types.name: Decision
entity_types.description: A decision that was taken and its reason. Not for: open questions. Examples: 'Ship in two phases', 'Adopt Postgres'.

entity_types.name: Risk
entity_types.description: Something that may go wrong, with its impact or mitigation. Not for: problems that already happened. Examples: 'Vendor delay may push the release'.

entity_types.name: Document
entity_types.description: A spec, report, proposal, plan or minute that can be cited. Not for: a meeting itself (Meeting). Examples: 'Technical design doc', 'Q3 roadmap'.

entity_types.name: Topic
entity_types.description: A subject or domain. LAST RESORT: only when nothing more specific fits. Not for: people, teams, projects or tasks. Examples: 'accessibility'.

edge_types.name: MemberOf
edge_types.description: A person belongs to a team or organization.

edge_types.name: Leads
edge_types.description: A person leads or manages a team, project or task.

edge_types.name: AssignedTo
edge_types.description: A task is assigned to a person or team.

edge_types.name: Owns
edge_types.description: A person or team is accountable for a project, document or deliverable.

edge_types.name: PartOf
edge_types.description: A task belongs to a project, a project to a larger project, a team to an organization, a milestone to a project.

edge_types.name: DependsOn
edge_types.description: A task, milestone or project cannot proceed without another.

edge_types.name: Blocks
edge_types.description: A risk or task prevents another task or milestone from progressing.

edge_types.name: DecidedIn
edge_types.description: A decision was taken in a meeting.

edge_types.name: Attends
edge_types.description: A person or team takes part in a meeting.

edge_types.name: ReportsTo
edge_types.description: A person reports to another person.

edge_types.name: Mitigates
edge_types.description: A task or decision reduces or handles a risk.

edge_types.name: Authored
edge_types.description: A person or team wrote a document.

edge_types.name: MentionedIn
edge_types.description: An entity is referenced in a document or meeting.

edge_types.name: RelatesTo
edge_types.description: LAST RESORT. Use only when two entities are clearly associated and no other relation type in the list fits. Never use it when a more specific type applies.

instructions: Team and project notes. Use the MOST SPECIFIC type: a ticket or to-do is a Task, a group inside a company is a Team, a customer or vendor is an Organization. Extract MemberOf/Leads for team structure, AssignedTo for ownership of tasks, PartOf and DependsOn for structure and ordering, DecidedIn for decisions taken in meetings, and Blocks/Mitigates for risks. Record due dates and dates of decisions when stated. Use only the listed relation types and prefer a specific one over RelatesTo.
